x: In the Junior events we saw Alan Law score a good double by winning the 100 and 220 yards, while Brian Trower was another dual winner in the 440 and 880 with Boreham giving him good assistance in both races.

Gregory won the 2 miles walk in 14 min. 12.4 secs., and this was our only other success except that our Junior team of Frank Kemp, Alan Law, Ian Forrester and John Benstead won the 4 x 110 yards Junior relay, beating Poly H. and the R.A.F., Halton, in 45.2 secs.

We won the Junior match fairly comfortably and Alan Law won the weight with a put of 45ft. 6ins. Alan also won the Junior long jump and once again proved what a tower of strength he is to our Club ranks.

The 300 yards handicap saw "Jock" Cameron, our new member from Coventry Godiva H., running well to get up off 8 yards with Don Newell showing improved form to finish 2nd and John Smith, a protege of Frank Elson, in 3rd place. Alan Law won the Weight handicap with D.

Childs in second place, and it looks as if we are building up a really strong section for next season. In the junior events we had Alan Law winning the 100 yds., also the weight, and in the latter we also had J.

The sprint events were 1st and 2nd string races and Ivan Mayers scored a good double when winning the 100 in 10.4 and the 220 in 22.5 secs. Alan Law was second in the other 100 yds. race, while D. Gordon was third for us in the 2nd 220 yards

In the Senior events, Dickey Barlett was 2nd, with John Benstead 3rd in the 220, with Alan Law 2nd in the Weight, and Len Bishop was 3rd in the 880 yds.
Gaworski won the Weight with 40ft. 11 ins., and was 3rd in the Discus with 117ft. 10½ins. Alan Law was 6th in the Weight, with D.

The County Pentathlon Championship was another event to be decided and in this Alan Law was the winner with a total of 1,302 pts As the events include 100 metres, 110 metres Hurdles, 1,500 metres, Pole Vault and Discus Throw, it will be seen that Alan did very well to win, and it looks as if we have…
Basil Walden, Pete Cornish and Alan Law all qualified for the 100 yds. final, but could not get placed in the first three, and Jim Heathfield also reached the 440 final.
Alan Law won the Weight, and H. Powell, the son of our old champion, George Powell, followed in his father's footsteps by winning the Javelin Throw.
Fleming, A.
Paris Schools meeting at the Wimbledon Park Track, Alan Law won the weight with a put of 44ft. 11¼ins., and at the same meeting our Junior team won the 1 mile medley relay open to clubs.
The three miles walk saw Gordon Doubleday a good winner from Syd James with our old veteran Charlie Sppechley 3rd. Alan Law won the weight handicap and with an allowance of 4ft.6ins did 42ft. 3ins.
I am now looking forward to the Kinnaird and hope we shall again make a good show. Alan Law is at Oxford but recovering from a strained back.

With two or three times reaching 23 feet 6 inches last year, there's no reason why you shouldn't find that extra six inches. Alan Law, G.

The winner's time was 22 mins. 56 secs. and it was pleasing to see our President a proud competitor. The sprint final was a very close affair, D. [illegible]arter, (5 yards) was just ahead of A. Law (7 yds), both being timed at 12.2secs.

Our Nigerian performer E.Bone took the High Jump from P.Luxon who had previously done the double with both the Javelin and Long Jump. Surprise winner of the Shot was Junior Alan Law. The meeting of the year from a domestic angle was of course the A.A.A.
